## Where I am

WaniKani level 27 as of 15 December 2024. About 1,140 kanji and 2,900 vocab words "known", meaning I recognise them
in WaniKani's font and freeze in a handwritten menu. Sat the JLPT N3 on 1 December 2024 at the Universidade de
Lisboa test centre, seat number 3N-0412.

Update February 2025: passed, 118/180. Reading section 41/60, my weakest.

## Method

- First 300 kanji with RTK keywords (Heisig), Sep 2023 to Jan 2024. Good for shapes, useless for readings.
- Switched to WaniKani lifetime (bought at $299 in the December sale) for radicals → kanji → vocab with readings.
- 45 minutes a day, split: 20 reviews in the morning, lessons at lunch, reading at night.

## Radicals that unlocked things

氵 water (three drops), 扌 hand, 言 speech, 糸 thread, 金 metal. Once 言 clicked, 語 読 話 説 all fell into place in
one week.

## Mnemonics I'm proud of

- 休 rest: a person leaning on a tree
- 森 forest: three trees, obviously
- 働 work: a person moving heavily, the most Japanese kanji ever
- 曜 weekday: a feathered bird on the sun, I picture a pigeon taking Monday off

## Reading practice

NHK News Web Easy three articles a week, Satori Reader on the tram, and Yotsuba&! volume 1, finished in March 2024
with a dictionary open. Film posters for [[黒澤明の構図]] are surprisingly good practice, all vertical text.

## Writing by hand

Genkōyōshi notebook, 10 minutes a day, stroke order from the Kanji Study app. Writing 必 correctly took me a month.

## Overflow into Anki

Leeches from WaniKani go into a separate Anki deck, settings in [[Anki deck settings]]. The scheduling theory is in
[[Spaced repetition intervals]].

## In the wild

Kyoto was the first real test: station names, temple signs, the ryokan's handwritten breakfast menu. Notes in
[[Kyoto]]. Read about 60% of the signs, guessed another 20%.
